findings.statement: JAK-STAT pathway activity is higher in inflamed or UC mucosa than control in all eight cohorts (for example t in GSE193677 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]). This supports the approved JAK inhibitors as a pathway already drug-targeted.

TNFa pathway activity is up in all eight cohorts (t in GSE206285 [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]); NFkB, MAPK, PI3K, TGFb, EGFR and Hypoxia are also up in all eight. Because nearly every inflammatory pathway is up together, the breadth is not specific. TNF is already drug-targeted.

STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts (t in GSE206285 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]), consistent with IL-6/IL-22/OSM-gp130 and JAK signalling. It is inferred from target genes, not from the STAT3 mRNA.

Androgen pathway activity is inconsistent: it is up in two cohorts and down in three, and falls strongly in GSE109142 (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-10.8]). p53 is down in three cohorts and up in none. Neither can be called a robust UC-wide signal.

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking, with up-regulation in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]) and genetic association. CXCR2 antagonists (reparixin Phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin and SX-682 Phase 2) exist but are not approved for UC, so this is an untapped axis.

In the single-cell data, neutrophils account for most CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed UC (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]), whereas the Smillie dataset, which has no neutrophils, assigns it to a small fraction of T/NK cells. The bulk CXCR2 increase is therefore an infiltrating neutrophil signal, not a change of tissue cells.

CXCL8 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come mainly from neutrophils (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]) when neutrophils are present. Without neutrophils, macrophages dominate (Smillie), so the cell of origin depends on the dataset.

CXCL8 to CXCR2 is a neutrophil-to-neutrophil autocrine/paracrine loop: sender Neutrophil CXCR4, receiver Neutrophil, with log2 change in inflamed versus uninflamed [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]. This is co-expression, not proof of signalling.

Neutrophil CXCL8 also pairs with the atypical receptor ACKR1 on ACKR1 endothelial cells, with log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.991]. This suggests an endothelial presentation route for neutrophil recruitment. It is co-expression only.

The hypothesised neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is weak in this dataset. Neutrophil OSM to IL6ST on LP fibroblasts has a low score and falls in inflamed tissue (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]). Only the Neutrophil PADI4 to LP fibroblast pair rises, from a score of zero in uninflamed tissue. Fibroblast OSM signalling is not supported as a dominant circuit here.

IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages is paired with IL1R2 on neutrophil states, for example Neutrophil PADI4 (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=1.168]). IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this pairing does not by itself indicate activating signalling. IL1B is targeted by canakinumab (approved for other indications) but is not an approved UC drug.

IDO1 is up in all eight cohorts and is mainly made by enterocytes in inflamed mucosa in the Gubatan data (share [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed_with_neutrophils.0.share=0.427]), with DC1 and macrophages in Smillie. Neutrophils contribute little. Epacadostat and linrodostat exist, but none is established in UC.

caveats: PROGENy and CollecTRI activities are inferred from bulk biopsy transcriptomes, and inflamed mucosa activates nearly all inflammatory pathways at once, so breadth across cohorts is weak evidence of specificity.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression in one single-cell dataset (Gubatan 2026) and are not proof of signalling. Neutrophil capture depends on the dissociation protocol.
Bulk increases in neutrophil genes such as CXCR2 and CXCL8 may reflect infiltrating cell abundance rather than a change in tissue cell programmes.
TREM1 had no ligand-receptor pair above threshold. IL-23 and integrin axes were not examined in detail here.
